- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast slightly to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.  
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model often fails to revert to historical mean — use 18-day rolling average as anchor for correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate upward momentum in bullish sentiment cycles — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.6 over last 7 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings > 0.5 in 3 days), model overfits short-term noise — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
